title: Sometimes a Team Just Needs a Win
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses what leaders should do when a team is stuck in a prolonged losing streak in the marketplace, arguing that morale requires an active intervention rather than just waiting for external conditions to improve. It reframes what counts as a win, suggesting that any collaborative achievement, not just a market victory, can restore a team's sense of competence and momentum. The piece offers concrete categories of manufactured wins: internal creative projects like launching a new process or website, charitable efforts such as renovating homes, and external competitions like community races. The underlying argument is that the experience of winning together, regardless of its source, is what sustains a team through a genuinely difficult stretch.
points: Sustained negative performance erodes team morale in ways that require active leadership intervention.
Waiting for external conditions to improve is described as hope rather than strategy.
A win can come from any collaborative outcome, not just market or competitive success.
Suggested sources of manufactured wins include new internal projects, charitable efforts, and external competitions.
Experiencing a win, regardless of its source, restores a struggling team's morale and momentum.
quotes: Maintaining the energy and enthusiasm required to succeed long-term is exceedingly difficult when teams aren't putting points on the board.
Waiting until the external tide turns and/or the performance roadblocks dissipate is more hope than strategy.
They know a team that is struggling needs a win, no matter where it comes from.
Creating something significant from scratch is just the ticket for a team that needs to post a victory.
Charitable efforts are another great place for the team to score an easy win.
Nothing feels better to a team that hasn't had a victory lately.
